title: Lipschitz Stokes pressure and bounded sensors

items.title: Bounded Stokes pressure sensors
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set. Put $Q:=L^2_0(D)=\{q\in L^2(D;\mathbb R):\int_Dq\,dx=0\}$ with the $L^2$ norm, and write $Q'$ for the continuous real dual of $Q$. A bounded Stokes pressure sensor on $D$ is a bounded real-linear functional $S:Q\to\mathbb R$, where bounded means that its operator norm $\|S\|_{Q'}:=\sup_{\|q\|_{L^2(D)}\le1}|S(q)|$ is finite. The reading of $S$ at a normalized pressure $q\in Q$ is $S(q)$.

items.title: Lipschitz stability of bounded Stokes pressure observations
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, and let $
u>0$. Set $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ with $\|v\|_V=\|
abla v\|_{L^2(D)}$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$ with the $L^2$ norm. For each $F\in V'$, let $(u_F,p_F)\in V	imes Q$ be the unique pair satisfying
$$2
u\int_D\varepsilon(u_F):\varepsilon(v)\,dx-\int_Dp_F\,\operatorname{div}v\,dx=F(v)\quad(v\in V),\qquad-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}u_F\,dx=0\quad(q\in Q),$$
where $V'$ is the continuous real dual of $V$ and $\varepsilon(u)=(
abla u+
abla u^T)/2$. Write $C_{m div}(D)$ for a finite constant in a bounded right inverse estimate $\operatorname{div}B_Dq=q$ and $\|
abla B_Dq\|_{L^2(D)}\le C_{m div}(D)\|q\|_{L^2(D)}$ for $q\in Q$. For a positive integer $m$ and bounded pressure sensors $S_1,\ldots,S_m\in Q'$, define $\mathcal O(F)=(S_1(p_F),\ldots,S_m(p_F))\in\mathbb R^m$. Then $F\mapsto p_F$ and $\mathcal O$ are real-linear, and for all $F,G\in V'$
$$\|\mathcal O(F)-\mathcal O(G)\|_{\mathbb R^m}\le 3C_{m div}(D)\left(\sum_{j=1}^m\|S_j\|_{Q'}^2ight)^{1/2}\|F-G\|_{V'},$$
where $\mathbb R^m$ has its Euclidean norm.

items.title: Gauge-invariant pressure sensor weights
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, with $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$. Take $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ and define $S_g(q):=\int_Dgq\,dx$ for $q\in Q$; this is a bounded pressure sensor. Put $\bar g:=|D|^{-1}\int_Dg\,dx$. On the normalized pressure space, $S_g=S_{g-\bar g}$. Whenever $p$ denotes an unnormalized pressure representative in a weak pressure term or sensor reading below, take $p\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$; a normalized pressure is denoted $q\in Q\subset L^2(D;\mathbb R)$. The weak Stokes pressure term $-\int_Dp\,\operatorname{div}v\,dx$ is unchanged by $p\mapsto p+c$ for $v\in V$ and $c\in\mathbb R$. The unnormalized sensor reading $\int_Dgp\,dx$ is unchanged under every pressure shift $p\mapsto p+c$ if and only if $\int_Dg\,dx=0$, equivalently $g\in Q$.

title: Lipschitz Stokes pressure and bounded sensors — Examples

items.title: A gradient load observed through Stokes pressure
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, and let $\nu>0$. Use $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ with gradient norm and $Q=L^2_0(D)$. Define $\bar x_1:=|D|^{-1}\int_Dx_1\,dx$ and $\phi(x):=x_1-\bar x_1$. The load $F_\phi(v):=-\int_D\phi\,\operatorname{div}v\,dx$ is the gradient forcing $\nabla\phi=e_1$ in the weak sense. The unique weak Stokes solution is $(u,p)=(0,\phi)$, and the bounded gauge-invariant sensor $S_\phi(q):=\int_D\phi q\,dx$ has reading $S_\phi(p)=\int_D\phi^2\,dx>0$.
